output.source_text: In a major key (e.g., C major), there are seven diatonic chords: C (I), Dm (ii), Em (iii), F (IV), G (V), Am (vi), and Bdim (vii°). The 7th chord built on the leading tone (vii°) is a diminished triad. Despite being one of the seven primary diatonic chords of the key, it is extremely rare in popular music.
